content.text: Every month, electricity bills arrive showing how much energy we've used. But how is electrical energy calculated? Understanding the relationship between power, time, and energy is essential for managing electricity costs and understanding how energy is transferred in circuits.
Electrical energy (E) = power (P) x time (t). Energy can be measured in joules (J) when using watts and seconds, or in kilowatt-hours (kWh) when using kilowatts and hours.

When calculating electricity costs, make sure power is in kW and time is in hours to get energy in kWh. Then multiply by the cost per kWh. Watch out for unit conversions — watts to kilowatts and minutes to hours.
